chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said, concerning a man who pledged collateral with another man and the pledged property was lost: “It is from the property of the pledger, and the pledgee may recover his money from him.”

key_terms.بِمَالِهِ: with his money, meaning the debt owed to the creditor
key_terms.رَهْنًا: pledged collateral given as security for a debt
key_terms.ٱلرَّاهِنِ: the pledger, the one who provides the collateral
key_terms.ٱلرَّهْنُ: the pledged property held as collateral
key_terms.ٱلْمُرْتَهِنُ: the pledgee, the one holding the collateral against a debt

ai.seo_question: Who bears the loss if pledged collateral is lost in a rahn transaction?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding pledged collateral (rahn) when the pledged item is lost. The loss is borne by the pledger, and the creditor holding the pledge retains the right to recover the debt owed to him.
